$comment: Built-in list prices in micro-USD per million tokens (1 USD = 1_000_000 micro-USD).
This is the BASELINE layer. Effective pricing is resolved in three layers:
1. this document — the floor, always present, never fails to load
2. the active price source (STRATOCLAVE_PRICE_SOURCE; "json" reads this file)
— a plugin may fetch live prices, e.g. from the AWS Price List API
3. admin overrides in the PricingConfig table — highest precedence
A key absent from every layer falls back to "default", which is Opus-priced:
an unpriced model must over-charge, never under-charge.
Models reference a key via `pricing_key` in defaults/models.json; models that share
a price tier share a key, so re-pricing a tier is one edit here.
A rate object may also carry `notes`; any other key is rejected as a typo.

fable.notes: Claude Fable 5 — $10/$50 per MTok, above the Opus tier. Cache rates follow the Anthropic ratio used for Opus (read = 0.1x input, write = 1.25x input).

gpt-5.notes: GPT-5.x on bedrock-mantle. Output priced at the Opus tier as a conservative default until an admin sets an exact rate.

gpt-5.6-sol.notes: Exact In-Region/Geo list price from the AWS Bedrock model card (Aug 2026): $4.40/$22.00 in/out, $0.44/$5.50 cache read/write.

gpt-5.6-terra.notes: Exact In-Region/Geo list price from the AWS Bedrock model card (Aug 2026): $2.20/$13.20 in/out, $0.22/$2.75 cache read/write.

grok.notes: xAI Grok 4.6 In-Region/Geo list price: $2.20/$6.60 in/out, $0.55 cache read. Bedrock publishes no cache-WRITE rate; the 1.25x-input premium the Anthropic tiers use is assumed as an UPPER BOUND so the ledger never under-charges.

gemma.notes: Gemma 4 31B (google.gemma-4-31b) on-demand list price at us-east-2, standard service tier: $0.14 in / $0.40 out per MTok. Source: AWS Price List API, AmazonBedrock, service_tier=standard, corroborated by the public Bedrock pricing page. Bedrock publishes no cache-READ or cache-WRITE rate for this model, so per the never-under-charge rule a cache read is charged at the full input rate and a cache write carries the 1.25x-input premium the Anthropic tiers use, both as upper bounds.

nemotron.notes: Bedrock publishes no list price. Defaults to the Opus tier for the same reason as gemma.

qwen.notes: Bedrock publishes no list price. Defaults to the Opus tier for the same reason as gemma.

default.notes: Conservative fallback (Opus-priced) so a model with no row never under-charges a budget.
